reviews.text: Not all bad. It’s just bad as a murder mystery. What does it say about a thriller if its best parts are not the actual murder or the clues that lead you to the killer, but the squabbling, grumbling interactions of a bored, middle-aged couple?
reviews.author: Sonali Kokra

reviews.text: It’s not fresh enough to be called original and not smart enough to be called a parody.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: I'm not criticizing character development or anything like that, I just kicked back... and watched a good movie.
reviews.author: Lonita Cook

reviews.text: With a plot reminiscent of Murder on the Orient Express, only this time on a Mediterranean yacht, Murder Mystery has a summer vibe that combines thriller and comedy.
reviews.author: Casey Cipriani

reviews.text: A good cast tries to carry this mediocre film.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: It would be welcome to see more movies between them in the same vein, even if Murder Mystery was a bit of an uninspired trek...
reviews.author: Luke Whiston

reviews.text: Murder Mystery is neither a comedy nor a mystery. It's just bad behavior masquerading as mass entertainment.
reviews.author: Amanda Greever

reviews.text: The problem with this movie is it's just not funny. I don't know if I even laughed one time.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: If you have 90 minutes to kill, Murder Mystery will tick the boxes for easy entertainment.
reviews.author: Lydia Gan

reviews.text: It's almost as if the creators couldn't be bothered to develop the scenario beyond a slapdash first draft.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: Little grey cells aren't required to enjoy this pleasant trip into the comedy-mystery genre. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Jennifer Aniston and Adam Sandler are no strangers to comedy, so they try their best. But most of their comic banter falls flat.
reviews.author: Betty Jo Tucker

reviews.text: ...a decent premise that's employed to passable (if entirely forgettable) effect...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: The best that can be said of Murder Mystery is that it's a mildly amusing experience that won't offend but will most certainly evaporate from the mind soon after.
reviews.author: Mark McPherson

reviews.text: Critics are right - the film isn't great.
reviews.author: Ani Bundel

reviews.text: The only mystery left to solve is how a comedy boasting an all-star cast can be so dull and lifeless. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: The biggest mystery soon becomes: why make this movie in the first place? Besides to give these hardworking actors an overseas vacation.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: The Aniston/Sandler spark we have seen before is somehow missing in this pedestrian dramedy. You expect more but you get less.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Some of the good things about this film is it's not way too long like some Netflix films. Also the presence of well-known actors like Adam Sandler and Jennifer Aniston give it more laughs.
reviews.author: Diana Saenger

reviews.text: Thanks to a deft, funny script by James Vanderbilt and brisk direction by Kyle Newacheck, this throwback comedy turns out to be an easygoing charmer.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: The film is not a milestone of cinematography but it entertains. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mauricio Nava

reviews.text: A mildly amusing whodunit that's just as irrelevant as Netflix's throwaway Adam Sandler comedies that have come before.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Murder Mystery benefits from the fact that it definitely doesn't take itself seriously. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Murder Mystery was a pleasant surprise and another terrific comedy showcase for Aniston.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Murder Mystery's predictability and cliches are comforting - which has entertainment value if you're not looking to be challenged for 90 minutes.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: The whole shebang is a moderately shoddy, microscopically amusing whodunit.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Watching Murder Mystery is a slog, and I still can't comprehend how the same dude who wrote Zodiac wrote this, and oh, did I mention this movie steals one of its final reveals from Legally Blonde?
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: Passable comic mystery has violence, swearing, sexual jokes.
reviews.author: Renee Schonfeld

reviews.text: Murder Mystery is an algorithm based comedy specifically created for distracted viewers and a clear symptom of Adam Sandler's catatonic and derivative comedy. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nicolás Ruiz

reviews.text: Murder Mystery is an easygoing movie where, for the first time in a long time, Sandler lets the audience in on the fun.
reviews.author: Eddie Strait

reviews.text: While it may be competently - if unexceptionally - made, the project basically struggles with being inventive.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: It's no Punch-Drunk Love, but it's on the better end of the spectrum when it comes to Sandler's streaming selections.
reviews.author: Karen Han

reviews.text: With much more tact and good taste than usual, Sandler and company offer a classic criminal comedy. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Kiko Vega

reviews.text: Watching "Murder Mystery" is a chore to endure and one you wouldn't want to have to sit through in public. Yet somehow, it still isn't the worst film to be released in 2019.
reviews.author: Matt Ward

reviews.text: Aniston and Sandler, paired before in 2011's Just Go With It, relax into their roles as if their only stake in Mystery is to enjoy the free trip to Italy and have fun running down cobblestones.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Forget the recycled rom-com gimmicks and oddball supporting roles, what gives this Netflix romp some joy is watching two comedy stars have fun.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Adam Sandler and Jennifer Aniston re-team in this comedy that's ridiculous in the best way.
reviews.author: Lauren Veneziani

reviews.text: the idea of reality being a form of pantomime that people can observe and commentate, as if they have nothing invested themselves and no skin in the game whatsoever, is what keeps this film enjoyable
reviews.author: Luke Buckmaster

reviews.text: If you find yourself liquored up in your living room over a long weekend, perhaps it's worth throwing on "Murder Mystery" as subtle background noise while you're napping the hangover away or doing the dishes.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: At the very least, I didn't regret watching it or hoping for my own swift death before the end credits rolled. Considering the glut of disposable direct-to-VOD projects being released in today's market, I'll take it as a small win.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: Murder Mystery is a bland crime-comedy that features Sandler on autopilot and struggles to deliver enough thrills to make it a worthwhile endeavor.
reviews.author: Chris Agar

reviews.text: Is Murder Mystery amusing? Not often. Is it intriguing? Not particularly.
reviews.author: Blake Goble

reviews.text: Murder Mystery is a seriously fun and wildly hilarious film that is sure to make you laugh.
reviews.author: Ashley Menzel

reviews.text: The first 20 minutes of Netflix's 'Murder Mystery' is some of Adam Sandler's funniest work in years. But then there's the rest of the film, which ranges from OK to silly.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Every Adam Sandler comedy abides by a trope as hoary as "the butler did it." At some point in the shenanigans, Sandler's schlub has gotta get a chance to prove he's the bravest boy in the world.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: The crime? A truly boring movie.
reviews.author: Anne Cohen

reviews.text: It would be uncomfortably cynical to assume that Sandler thinks these novocaine-like comedies are what common people want to watch, but the guy doesn't leave us much choice.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Still, the movie proves a cheery enough diversion, during a summer movie season leaden with underwhelming blockbuster offerings.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: The whodunit comedy doesn't do [Adam] Sandler or co-star Jennifer Aniston too many favors.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: The Aniston-Sandler pair is not enough to save this parody of mystery films (and novels). [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Janire Zurbano

reviews.text: Even grading on a curve, though, Murder Mystery is a tired, bordering on tiresome endeavor -- feeling like the pilot for a not-very-good TV show -- as well as a reminder that Netflix's content buffet caters to all kinds of tastes.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Murder Mystery isn't high cinema, but it does showcase how Sandler can work really well with certain co-leads -- and Jennifer Aniston is on that short list.
reviews.author: Matt Fowler

reviews.text: Adam Sandler is a genius, sure. But I'd love it if he were to smarten up, too.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: For something that's top of the landing page, thus doesn't even require thumb movement, Murder Mystery is surprisingly entertaining.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: It's just the kind of movie to pop on one night when you're looking for something fun, silly, and a little mysterious.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Just entertaining enough to make you wish it was actually good.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Capably directed by Kyle Newacheck from a suitably twisty-turny script by James Vanderbilt, it serves its purpose as a lighthearted comedy.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Murder Mystery is a breezy and occasionally funny slice of light entertainment. That's not a bad look for Sandler.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: It's not the slam-dunk project it initially appears to be, but it's intermittently entertaining.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: If you've seen an Adam Sandler movie anytime this century, you know what you're getting, and it's not interesting or funny.
reviews.author: Dirk Libbey

reviews.text: Adam Sandler's recent Netflix special, 100% Fresh, is maybe the funniest thing you'll see all year. But his rotten streak gets reset with this flat, lifeless dud.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Sandler has had some misses over the past few years, but this film will remind you why you loved him in the first place.
reviews.author: Jenna Busch

reviews.text: Murder Mystery... isn't going to dispel the longstanding rumor that the Sandman mostly makes movies as an excuse to go on paid vacations, using his Happy Madison production shingle as a personal travel agency
reviews.author: Ignatiy Vishnevetsky

reviews.text: Although it gets off to a bit of a shaky start, the comedic thriller Murder Mystery manages to settle into an entertaining groove once the titular game is afoot.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Aniston and Sandler have a goofy, relaxed rapport that is often amusing despite the film's best efforts to smother any sign of verve.
reviews.author: Elisabeth Vincentelli

reviews.text: Aniston, not for the first time, seems more engaged and wide-awake than her material, and you can sense her mental gears grinding away as she tests out bits of business and digs for stray moments of comic gold. None, alas, are forthcoming.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Murder on the Bore-ient Express.
reviews.author: John DeFore

reviews.text: Murder Mystery is a satisfying standout, albeit one that exists in a field with a very low bar.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: No comedian stays great forever. But when you see how effective Adam Sandler can be when putting forth even a scintilla of skill, that's why these vending-machine movies - now complete with vending-machine titles - continue to rankle so much.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

synopsis: A New York cop and his wife go on a European vacation to reinvigorate the spark in their marriage. A chance encounter leads to them being framed for the murder of an elderly billionaire.
